items.title: My agents made a Photoshop equivalent in 8 hours
items.why_it_matters: An indie developer used coding agents to build a functional Photoshop clone in just 8 hours, sharing the entire codebase on GitHub. This shows how fast a complex, interactive UI can be scaffolded when you focus on directing the AI rather than writing every line of CSS. This week, you can clone the repository, run it locally, and inspect their prompt structure to see how they directed the AI to build the canvas and layer management systems.

items.title: Show HN: Hacker News Client with Claude Code and Codex Integration
items.why_it_matters: An indie developer built Rundown, a desktop Hacker News client, specifically using Claude Code and Codex to summarize long discussion threads and let users chat with the posts. It is a real-world example of using the exact tools in your stack to parse, filter, and summarize external web content. This week, you can look at their integration code on GitHub to see how they structured the prompts that summarize long comment threads, and adapt that logic directly into your AI-ingest tool.

items.title: Show HN: Claude Code Skills – Solving context bloat
items.why_it_matters: This open-source starter kit introduces "skills" to Claude Code to help manage context bloat, which is a common issue when letting AI do the heavy lifting on larger projects. It allows you to package repetitive commands and context into reusable skills so the AI doesn't waste tokens re-learning your project structure. This week, you can clone the kit and write a custom skill for your Supabase database schema so Claude Code instantly knows your table structures without you having to paste them in every session.

items.title: Show HN: Metis – An agent harness pushing DeepSeek to Opus-tier coding (82%)
items.why_it_matters: Metis is an open-source agent harness designed to run DeepSeek models with an iterative feedback loop, achieving coding benchmarks comparable to Claude 3.5 Opus. Since you previously found massive cost savings by delegating heavy coding tasks to cheaper models, this harness provides a structured way to do it without losing quality. This week, you can download the Metis repository and run a test prompt to see if it can generate a Next.js component for your AI-ingest project using DeepSeek instead of burning your Claude API limits.

items.title: Show HN: dmx – MCP server for adding configurable, gated loops to coding agents
items.why_it_matters: This Model Context Protocol (MCP) server lets you add configurable, human-in-the-loop gates to your coding agents, preventing them from running infinite loops and wasting your API tokens. Because you use Claude Code, you can easily plug this in to keep a tighter leash on your agent's execution steps. This week, you can install the dmx MCP server and configure a rule that forces Claude Code to ask for your manual approval before it executes more than three consecutive terminal commands.

items.title: Show HN: Agentify Chat – E2E-Encrypted Remote Chat for Codex, Claude, Grok CLIs
items.why_it_matters: Agentify Chat is an end-to-end encrypted web interface that acts as a remote control for terminal-based AI tools like Codex and Claude Code. If you find directing your AI-driven builds entirely inside a terminal window restrictive, this tool lets you interact with those same local CLI tools through a clean browser UI. This week, you can clone the repository, link it to your local Codex or Claude Code CLI, and try directing your next Next.js feature build from the browser interface.
